title: Wire the SkinnedMeshRenderer adapter into the live runtime/editor preview path for a demonstrable idle/walk
description:
## Summary
Wire the validated `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer` into the live preview path and ensure every generated mesh-asset item is also attached to the resolved semantic rig bone instead of remaining a static root child. The preview must present one coherent animated character hierarchy: generated implicit surface skinned by the CreatureRig plus rigid mesh-asset parts parented to their resolved part bones.

## User Mandate
A real generated creature must render through the established skinned presentation path. Mesh parts must follow their respective bones; no mesh part may remain a static sibling of the rig while the rest of the creature animates. The implementation must remain compatible with the separate external movement/animation rig.

## Scope
- Keep `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer` responsible for the implicit welded surface.
- For each generated `GeometryItem` with `RigBinding`, resolve `SourcePartId + IsMirrored` through `SemanticBoneResolver` to the already-built `CreatureRig` and parent the generated mesh-asset presentation object to that exact bone while preserving its world-space rest placement.
- Preserve existing `RigidMeshWeightAuthoring` data as the binding truth; the editor presentation should not invent a second attachment rule.
- Maintain structural preview ownership and teardown.
- Preserve source mesh and generated rest geometry.
- Do not add per-frame rebinding or procedural regeneration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A real generated creature renders through the existing SkinnedMeshRenderer path with its implicit surface bound once.
- Every rendered mesh-asset item has a resolved rig bone parent and follows that bone under a controlled pose.
- Mirrored mesh assets follow the mirrored semantic bone.
- No static mesh-asset object remains attached only to the preview root.
- Rebuild/clear leaves no orphaned presentation objects.
- Per-frame animation changes transforms only; no mesh/weight/bindpose rebuild.

## Validation
Run focused Editor preview tests plus PlayMode tests against `dinus_uprightus` or an equivalent real generated creature. Explicitly pose one body/limb bone and verify its mesh-asset children move with it while unrelated mesh assets remain fixed. Run dotnet builds and `git diff --check`.

## Residual performance note
Parenting a rigid mesh asset to a bone is intentionally cheaper than introducing another SkinnedMeshRenderer for a one-bone object. Do not convert rigid accessory geometry into a second per-frame skinning path unless evidence requires it.

## Status
InProgress — implementation landed for implicit-surface live binding and rigid mesh-asset bone parenting; Unity/generated-creature validation remains the closure gate.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Original implicit-surface live preview integration evidence (2026-09-06): CreaturePreviewController built CreatureRig, applied rest pose once, created CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer, and enabled its SMR. Focused PlayMode and EditMode gates passed in the original slice. The original acceptance did not require mesh-asset objects to follow runtime bones.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Follow-up from user visual validation: generated mesh-asset presentation objects were still parented directly to the preview root, so they could not follow their RigBinding bone when the skeleton posed. Corrected CreaturePreviewController to resolve each RigBinding SourcePartId/IsMirrored through SemanticBoneResolver and parent the mesh object to the exact rig bone while preserving world-space rest placement. This is intentionally rigid parenting for one-bone accessories; do not introduce a second per-frame skinning path. Unity validation remains required.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Binding hardening (2026-09-07): editor implicit-surface rig inference now consumes the exact ResolvedCreatureSnapshot produced for the generation result instead of re-inferencing from the raw CreatureDefinition. This removes a duplicate resolution/derivation path at the presentation boundary while retaining definition input only for the existing SDF-based influence-domain resolver contract.
